# zmux Wire Examples

Status: informative. Every byte in this document is generated by
`tools/build_wire.py` and checked by `tools/validate_assets.py`, which
re-encodes each example from the JSON block above it, decodes the bytes back,
and recomputes the key-schedule vectors. Do not edit this file by hand.

Each example shows the JSON description (the frame objects of TRACES.md
Section 6, byte strings in hex), a field table, and the complete record
(`Size` followed by the frames).


## 1. Transport parameters

### 1.1 Transport parameters of a zmux endpoint

The first record of a bootstrap pipe: QX_TRANSPORT_PARAMETERS with the recommended values of SPEC.md Section 5.3, `max_incoming_uni_streams` configured to 256 (unset, it would send 16 and raise the limit to 256 on the first accept, SPEC.md Section 8.5 rule 4), `zmux_max_lanes` with Max Lanes 258 and a Lane Key (a fixed example here; an endpoint chooses it at random for each session, MULTIPATH.md Section 3.6), and one GREASE parameter (31 x 3 + 27 = 120).

<!-- zmux-example tp-zmux-default -->
```json
{"id": "tp-zmux-default", "record": [{"type": "QX_TRANSPORT_PARAMETERS", "params": [{"id": "max_idle_timeout", "value": 30000}, {"id": "initial_max_data", "value": 1048576}, {"id": "initial_max_stream_data_bidi_local", "value": 262144}, {"id": "initial_max_stream_data_bidi_remote", "value": 262144}, {"id": "initial_max_stream_data_uni", "value": 262144}, {"id": "initial_max_streams_bidi", "value": 256}, {"id": "initial_max_streams_uni", "value": 256}, {"id": "reset_stream_at", "value": null}, {"id": "zmux_goaway", "value": null}, {"id": "zmux_preamble", "value": 4096}, {"id": "zmux_priority", "value": null}, {"id": "zmux_pipe_ack", "value": null}, {"id": "zmux_max_lanes", "value": {"max_lanes": 258, "lane_key": "8d2f6a01c7e4b35a90f1d26e4b7c0a39"}}, {"id": "max_record_size", "value": 65535}, {"id": 120, "raw": "9a7b"}]}]}
```

### 1.2 Transport parameters of a plain QMux peer

What the Rust `qmux` crate sends: only QUIC parameters, zero values omitted. A zmux endpoint receiving this runs the session in plain QMux mode (SPEC.md Section 13).

## 2. Core frames

### 2.1 Opening a stream with a preamble

The first frame of stream 0: a preamble with OPEN_INFO "example.com:443", PRIORITY urgency 1, and a GREASE TLV (type 0x21, empty), then 5 bytes of data and FIN. Offset 0 is implicit (no OFF bit).

<!-- zmux-example stream-open-preamble -->
```json
{"id": "stream-open-preamble", "record": [{"type": "STREAM", "id": 0, "off": 0, "data": "16010f6578616d706c652e636f6d3a343433020120210068656c6c6f", "fin": true}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `1f` | 31 |
| Type | `0b` | 0xb STREAM (LEN|FIN) |
| Stream ID | `00` | 0 |
| Length | `1c` | 28 |
| Stream Data | `16 01 0f 65 78 61 6d 70 6c 65 2e 63 6f 6d 3a 34 34 33 02 01 ... (28 bytes)` | 28 bytes |

```hex
1f0b001c16010f6578616d706c652e636f6d3a343433020120210068656c6c6f
```

### 2.2 First record with early data

A client whose application declares the peer to be a zmux endpoint opens stream 0 before the peer's parameters arrive (SPEC.md Section 6.1.2): after its QX_TRANSPORT_PARAMETERS (abbreviated here to initial_max_data) comes the PIPE_ACK fence, one entry for pipe 0, lane 0, Position 0, ACK Delay 0, then the STREAM frame with the preamble (GREASE TLV) and 3 bytes of data, within the floor of 4096 bytes. A plain QMux peer closes at the PIPE_ACK and processes nothing after it.

<!-- zmux-example early-data -->
```json
{"id": "early-data", "record": [{"type": "QX_TRANSPORT_PARAMETERS", "params": [{"id": "initial_max_data", "value": 1048576}]}, {"type": "PIPE_ACK", "entries": [{"pipe": 0, "lane": 0, "position": 0, "delay": 0}]}, {"type": "STREAM", "id": 0, "off": 0, "data": "022100474554", "fin": true}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `21` | 33 |
| Type | `ff 51 53 30 0d 0a 0d 0a` | 0x3f5153300d0a0d0a QX_TRANSPORT_PARAMETERS |
| Length | `06` | 6 |
|   initial_max_data: ID | `04` | 0x4 |
|   initial_max_data: Length | `04` | 4 |
|   initial_max_data: Value | `80 10 00 00` | 1048576 |
| Type | `8b 2b 3e eb` | 0xb2b3eeb PIPE_ACK |
| Entry Count | `01` | 1 |
|   Pipe ID | `00` | 0 |
|   Lane | `00` | 0 |
|   Position | `00` | 0 |
|   ACK Delay (us) | `00` | 0 |
| Type | `0b` | 0xb STREAM (LEN|FIN) |
| Stream ID | `00` | 0 |
| Length | `06` | 6 |
| Stream Data | `02 21 00 47 45 54` | 6 bytes |

```hex
21ff5153300d0a0d0a060404801000008b2b3eeb01000000000b000602210047
4554
```

### 2.3 Continuing a stream

Stream 4 data at offset 1200, followed by a second frame for stream 0 that omits its Length and therefore runs to the end of the record.

<!-- zmux-example stream-continue -->
```json
{"id": "stream-continue", "record": [{"type": "STREAM", "id": 4, "off": 1200, "data": "6d6f72652064617461", "fin": false}, {"type": "STREAM", "id": 0, "off": 27, "data": "7461696c", "fin": false, "has_len": false}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `15` | 21 |
| Type | `0e` | 0xe STREAM (OFF|LEN) |
| Stream ID | `04` | 4 |
| Offset | `44 b0` | 1200 |
| Length | `09` | 9 |
| Stream Data | `6d 6f 72 65 20 64 61 74 61` | 9 bytes |
| Type | `0c` | 0xc STREAM (OFF) |
| Stream ID | `00` | 0 |
| Offset | `1b` | 27 |
| Stream Data | `74 61 69 6c` | 4 bytes |


### 2.6 STOP_SENDING answered by RESET_STREAM

The peer stops stream 1 with ZMUX_CANCELLED; the sender answers with the same code.

<!-- zmux-example stop-and-reset -->
```json
{"id": "stop-and-reset", "record": [{"type": "STOP_SENDING", "id": 1, "code": 1514995713}, {"type": "RESET_STREAM", "id": 1, "code": 1514995713, "final_size": 4000}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `16` | 22 |
| Type | `05` | 0x5 STOP_SENDING |
| Stream ID | `01` | 1 |
| Application Error Code | `c0 00 00 00 5a 4d 00 01` | 1514995713 |
| Type | `04` | 0x4 RESET_STREAM |
| Stream ID | `01` | 1 |
| Application Error Code | `c0 00 00 00 5a 4d 00 01` | 1514995713 |
| Final Size | `4f a0` | 4000 |

```hex
160501c00000005a4d00010401c00000005a4d00014fa0
```

### 2.7 RESET_STREAM_AT protecting a preamble

Stream 0 reset with ZMUX_PROXY_CONNECTION_REFUSED; the first 19 bytes (the preamble) stay reliable (EXTENSIONS.md Section 4.5).

<!-- zmux-example reset-stream-at -->
```json
{"id": "reset-stream-at", "record": [{"type": "RESET_STREAM_AT", "id": 0, "code": 1514995973, "final_size": 24, "reliable_size": 19}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `0c` | 12 |
| Type | `24` | 0x24 RESET_STREAM_AT |
| Stream ID | `00` | 0 |
| Application Error Code | `c0 00 00 00 5a 4d 01 05` | 1514995973 |
| Final Size | `18` | 24 |
| Reliable Size | `13` | 19 |

```hex
0c2400c00000005a4d01051813
```

### 2.12 PADDING around a frame

PADDING is one zero byte per frame.

<!-- zmux-example padding -->
```json
{"id": "padding", "record": [{"type": "PADDING", "count": 3}, {"type": "MAX_DATA", "max": 2048}, {"type": "PADDING", "count": 2}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `08` | 8 |
| PADDING | `00 00 00` | 3 x 0x00 |
| Type | `10` | 0x10 MAX_DATA |
| Maximum Data | `48 00` | 2048 |
| PADDING | `00 00` | 2 x 0x00 |

```hex
080000001048000000
```

## 3. Negotiated features

### 3.1 GOAWAY

Final GOAWAY after the fence: streams of the receiver with index 6 or more (bidirectional) and 0 or more (unidirectional) were not processed.

<!-- zmux-example goaway -->
```json
{"id": "goaway", "record": [{"type": "GOAWAY", "max_bidi": 6, "max_uni": 0, "code": 0}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `07` | 7 |
| Type | `99 11 f4 3e` | 0x1911f43e GOAWAY |
| Maximum Bidirectional Streams | `06` | 6 |
| Maximum Unidirectional Streams | `00` | 0 |
| Application Protocol Error Code | `00` | 0 |

```hex
079911f43e060000
```

Stream 4, sequence 2, urgency 0, incremental.

```json
{"id": "priority-update", "record": [{"type": "PRIORITY_UPDATE", "id": 4, "seq": 2, "urgency": 0, "incremental": true}]}
```

| Sequence Number | `02` | 2 |
| Priority | `10` | urgency 0, incremental 1 |

```hex
07873d08cf040210
```

## 4. Multipath

### 4.1 PIPE_JOIN in band

The initiator joins uplink pipe 2 of the session whose locator is "LOCAL", using the test keys of Section 6; a STREAM frame follows in the same record (0-RTT).

<!-- zmux-example pipe-join -->
```json
{"id": "pipe-join", "record": [{"type": "PIPE_JOIN", "locator": "4c4f43414c", "pipe": 2, "direction": "up", "carrier_bound": false, "standby": false, "fate_group": 0, "priority": 0, "token": "aded106775c33141fb8864f9877f2c22"}, {"type": "STREAM", "id": 0, "off": 0, "data": "006561726c79", "fin": true}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `27` | 39 |
| Type | `9a 24 de 36` | 0x1a24de36 PIPE_JOIN |
| Locator Length | `05` | 5 |
| Session Locator | `4c 4f 43 41 4c` | b'LOCAL' |
| Pipe ID | `02` | 2 |
| Flags | `00` | direction up |
| Fate Group | `00` | 0 |
| Priority | `00` | 0 |
| Join Token | `ad ed 10 67 75 c3 31 41 fb 88 64 f9 87 7f 2c 22` | 16 bytes |
| Type | `0b` | 0xb STREAM (LEN|FIN) |
| Stream ID | `00` | 0 |
| Length | `06` | 6 |
| Stream Data | `00 65 61 72 6c 79` | 6 bytes |

```hex

0006006561726c79
```

### 4.2 PIPE_ACK

Positions of inbound pipes 0 and 2 with their acknowledgement delays in microseconds; pipe 2 has a second lane, acknowledged in an entry of its own (MULTIPATH.md Sections 2.5 and 6.2). Entries are in increasing (Pipe ID, Lane) order.

<!-- zmux-example pipe-ack -->
```json
{"id": "pipe-ack", "record": [{"type": "PIPE_ACK", "entries": [{"pipe": 0, "lane": 0, "position": 1048576, "delay": 1500}, {"pipe": 2, "lane": 0, "position": 65600, "delay": 250}, {"pipe": 2, "lane": 1, "position": 401920, "delay": 250}]}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `1d` | 29 |
| Type | `8b 2b 3e eb` | 0xb2b3eeb PIPE_ACK |
| Entry Count | `03` | 3 |
|   Pipe ID | `00` | 0 |
|   Lane | `00` | 0 |
|   Position | `80 10 00 00` | 1048576 |
|   ACK Delay (us) | `45 dc` | 1500 |
|   Pipe ID | `02` | 2 |
|   Lane | `00` | 0 |
|   Position | `80 01 00 40` | 65600 |
|   ACK Delay (us) | `40 fa` | 250 |
|   Pipe ID | `02` | 2 |
|   Lane | `01` | 1 |
|   Position | `80 06 22 00` | 401920 |
|   ACK Delay (us) | `40 fa` | 250 |

```hex
1d8b2b3eeb0300008010000045dc02008001004040fa02018006220040fa
```

### 4.3 First record of a lane

The writer of pipe 2 opens lane 1 of it on a new stream of the connection that carries the pipe's lane 0 (MULTIPATH.md Section 5.8). The record holds only PIPE_LANE, with the receiver's Lane Key from the `zmux_max_lanes` example of Section 1.1; the writer sends nothing else on the lane until a PIPE_ACK confirms it. The lane's position counts from this record's first byte.

<!-- zmux-example pipe-lane -->
```json
{"id": "pipe-lane", "record": [{"type": "PIPE_LANE", "lane_key": "8d2f6a01c7e4b35a90f1d26e4b7c0a39", "pipe": 2, "lane": 1}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `16` | 22 |
| Type | `ba 05 a1 c9` | 0x3a05a1c9 PIPE_LANE |
| Lane Key | `8d 2f 6a 01 c7 e4 b3 5a 90 f1 d2 6e 4b 7c 0a 39` | 16 bytes |
| Pipe ID | `02` | 2 |
| Lane | `01` | 1 |

```hex
16ba05a1c98d2f6a01c7e4b35a90f1d26e4b7c0a390201
```

### 4.4 PIPE_PING, PIPE_STATUS, PIPE_ABANDON

Probe; ask the peer to use its outbound direction of pipe 3 as a less-preferred tier (priority 10, available, sequence 1) and pipe 5 only on failover (standby, priority 0); abandon pipe 2 after a failure.

<!-- zmux-example pipe-control -->
```json
{"id": "pipe-control", "record": [{"type": "PIPE_PING"}, {"type": "PIPE_STATUS", "pipe": 3, "seq": 1, "status": "available", "priority": 10}, {"type": "PIPE_STATUS", "pipe": 5, "seq": 1, "status": "standby", "priority": 0}, {"type": "PIPE_ABANDON", "pipe": 2, "code": 694836213}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `1d` | 29 |
| Type | `a6 9b 43 e6` | 0x269b43e6 PIPE_PING |
| Type | `a2 7b 28 11` | 0x227b2811 PIPE_STATUS |
| Pipe ID | `03` | 3 |
| Sequence Number | `01` | 1 |
| Status | `00` | 0 (available) |
| Priority | `0a` | 10 |
| Type | `a2 7b 28 11` | 0x227b2811 PIPE_STATUS |
| Pipe ID | `05` | 5 |
| Sequence Number | `01` | 1 |
| Status | `01` | 1 (standby) |
| Priority | `00` | 0 |
| Type | `a3 b3 5b 74` | 0x23b35b74 PIPE_ABANDON |
| Pipe ID | `02` | 2 |
| Error Code | `a9 6a 5b f5` | 0x296a5bf5 ZMUX_PIPE_FAILED |

```hex
1da69b43e6a27b28110301000aa27b281105010100a3b35b7402a96a5bf5
```

### 4.5 PIPE_JOIN with a priority request

The initiator joins downlink pipe 4 and states its initial request for the acceptor's outbound direction of it (MULTIPATH.md Sections 5.1 and 9): standby (flag 0x08), priority 10. Sent out of band, the frame alone (Type through Join Token) is the value of the `Zmux-Pipe-Join` header, 40 characters; it is shown here in a record like the other examples.

<!-- zmux-example pipe-join-priority -->
```json
{"id": "pipe-join-priority", "record": [{"type": "PIPE_JOIN", "locator": "4c4f43414c", "pipe": 4, "direction": "down", "carrier_bound": false, "standby": true, "fate_group": 0, "priority": 10, "token": "952026317bf3ae451d827d5d875fe9c7"}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `1e` | 30 |
| Type | `9a 24 de 36` | 0x1a24de36 PIPE_JOIN |
| Locator Length | `05` | 5 |
| Session Locator | `4c 4f 43 41 4c` | b'LOCAL' |
| Pipe ID | `04` | 4 |
| Flags | `09` | direction down, standby |
| Fate Group | `00` | 0 |
| Priority | `0a` | 10 |
| Join Token | `95 20 26 31 7b f3 ae 45 1d 82 7d 5d 87 5f e9 c7` | 16 bytes |

```hex
1e9a24de36054c4f43414c0409000a952026317bf3ae451d827d5d875fe9c7
```

## 5. Resume

### 5.1 First record of a rejoined pipe

After a suspension the initiator joins bidirectional pipe 6. Its first record carries, after the PIPE_JOIN, a complete PIPE_ACK snapshot (MULTIPATH.md Section 5.2): every inbound pipe that is not retired and has a position, the failed pipe 2 included, so the peer learns at once what arrived (RESUME.md Section 5). The PIPE_PING asks for the peer's complete snapshot in return.

<!-- zmux-example rejoin-record -->
```json
{"id": "rejoin-record", "record": [{"type": "PIPE_JOIN", "locator": "4c4f43414c", "pipe": 6, "direction": "bidi", "carrier_bound": false, "standby": false, "fate_group": 0, "priority": 0, "token": "62b9b2187c6d5847e999b222ef1e497f"}, {"type": "PIPE_ACK", "entries": [{"pipe": 0, "lane": 0, "position": 4096, "delay": 0}, {"pipe": 2, "lane": 0, "position": 77, "delay": 0}]}, {"type": "PIPE_PING"}]}
```

| Field | Bytes | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Record Size | `31` | 49 |
| Type | `9a 24 de 36` | 0x1a24de36 PIPE_JOIN |
| Locator Length | `05` | 5 |
| Session Locator | `4c 4f 43 41 4c` | b'LOCAL' |
| Pipe ID | `06` | 6 |
| Flags | `02` | direction bidi |
| Fate Group | `00` | 0 |
| Priority | `00` | 0 |
| Join Token | `62 b9 b2 18 7c 6d 58 47 e9 99 b2 22 ef 1e 49 7f` | 16 bytes |
| Type | `8b 2b 3e eb` | 0xb2b3eeb PIPE_ACK |
| Entry Count | `02` | 2 |
|   Pipe ID | `00` | 0 |
|   Lane | `00` | 0 |
|   Position | `50 00` | 4096 |
|   ACK Delay (us) | `00` | 0 |
|   Pipe ID | `02` | 2 |
|   Lane | `00` | 0 |
|   Position | `40 4d` | 77 |
|   ACK Delay (us) | `00` | 0 |
| Type | `a6 9b 43 e6` | 0x269b43e6 PIPE_PING |

```hex
319a24de36054c4f43414c0602000062b9b2187c6d5847e999b222ef1e497f8b
2b3eeb0200005000000200404d00a69b43e6
```

## 7. First bytes of foreign protocols

The incremental first-record check of SPEC.md Section 6.2 rejects these prefixes at the byte shown.

| Input | First bytes | Rejected at byte |
|---|---|---|
| legacy zmux preface | `5a 4d 55 58 01` | 3 |
| HTTP/1.1 request | `47 45 54 20 2f 20` | 3 |
| HTTP/2 preface | `50 52 49 20 2a 20` | 3 |
| TLS ClientHello | `16 03 01` | 2 |
| SSH banner | `53 53 48 2d 32 2e` | 3 |

A listener decides on a zmux first record at the byte shown (MULTIPATH.md Section 5.5); the PIPE_LANE alternative applies only to a stream of a known carrier connection; elsewhere this record (Size 22, too small for a join) is rejected at its first frame-type byte.

| First record | Carrier | First bytes | Decided at byte | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QX_TRANSPORT_PARAMETERS | any | `09 ff 51 53 30 0d` | 9 | session |
| PIPE_JOIN | any | `1e 9a 24 de 36 05` | 5 | join |
| PIPE_LANE | stream of a known connection | `16 ba 05 a1 c9 8d` | 5 | lane |
| PIPE_LANE | any | `16 ba 05 a1 c9 8d` | 2 | reject |
